state:
- S2 and S4 remain unmatched systems: oxidative cytarabine-residual metabolism and DHODH-linked differentiation are each summarized accurately, yet nothing in either study shows residual cells are selectively DHODH-dependent. Insert a go/no-go in the same residual, bulk, and normal specimens: a reference DHODH inhibitor must shift dihydroorotate/orotate and induce genotype-confirmed maturation in the residual subset before any atovaquone phenotype is attributed to that context.
- The prespecified “salvage-low” gate uses labeled-uridine incorporation, which tracks uptake and cell-cycle state rather than dependence on de novo synthesis. Define salvage limitation by de novo-versus-salvage flux partitioning or by growth/differentiation dependence on uridine during reference DHODH inhibition, and keep incorporation as a covariate.
- The decisive tools are unnamed and lack an abort rule. Specify the respiratory-chain-independent DHODH ortholog, localization, expression window, and proof that pyrimidine restoration leaves complex III and ubiquinone inhibition intact; set the unbound-exposure ceiling from verified clinical unbound Cmax; and state that if pyrimidine pools fall only together with ATP collapse, or if the rescues fail against the reference DHODH inhibitor, the atovaquone test is uninterpretable and stops.
